problems.statement: A self-reinforcing staffing loop is the core problem: vacancies lead to agency use, which loads permanent RNs with charge and orientation shifts, which drives resignations (lagged about 2 quarters), which raises vacancies and agency use again.
The agency cost tripling is mainly a volume problem (77% of the increase), with the rate effect (23%) mechanically driven by the contract escalator tied to the state wage index.

Larchmere's pay scale fell behind the market (101% to 91% of regional median) after 3% raises against 9.4% and 7.9% market increases, which is a real contributing origin of attrition but a secondary one.

The client's framing, that this is an external market problem driven by St. Brennan's poaching, is largely rejected: the vacancy and resignation rise began in early 2024, well before St. Brennan's opened in March 2026, and only 19 of 98 known leavers went there.
The 4 West pilot failed, as the CNO believes, and shows that workload relief does not reduce attrition.

Workload relief on 4 West worked: exhaustion fell, charge-plus-orientation load fell by more than half, and resignations fell from 4 to 1 per quarter while matched units stayed flat or rose. The CNO's end-of-Q1 read missed the lag, since leavers had already given notice.

A $15,000 sign-on bonus funded by suspending charge and preceptor differentials would worsen the loop by cutting pay for the overloaded group and adding preceptorship load, while the 2025 bonus did not reduce vacancy and had late attrition.
Time-to-hire and recruiting speed are a bottleneck.
Agency use harms patient safety (falls with injury).
Contract terms are a cost lever: the Vantage escalator and above-market rates (other vendors 6-8% lower) with renewal due 2027-01-01 offer a near-term saving.

causalClaims.to: Charge and orientation burden on permanent RNs
Loss of charge-qualified RNs and more attrition

actions.action: Reduce permanent-RN charge and orientation load by extending the 4 West model (dedicated educators or orientation owners, charge caps with float backfill) to the highest-agency units first.
actions.rationale: The only intervention with matched-comparison evidence of reducing exhaustion and resignations, and it targets the loop's main mechanism.

actions.action: Renegotiate or re-tender the Vantage contract before the 2027-01-01 renewal (remove the wage-index escalator, use the 6-8% lower competing quotes).
actions.rationale: Cheap, controllable and time-bound saving on the 23% rate component.

actions.action: Reject the funding of the sign-on bonus by suspending charge and preceptor differentials.
actions.rationale: It cuts pay for the most overloaded, most flight-prone group and adds preceptorship load, which could accelerate the loop.

actions.action: Run a $15,000 sign-on bonus campaign as designed.
actions.rationale: The 2025 bonus did not lower vacancy, had post-clawback attrition, and new hires add preceptor load before retention is fixed.

actions.action: Adjust pay for the 2-8 year tenure charge/preceptor-qualified group, and consider retention (not sign-on) incentives tied to staying.
actions.rationale: The pay gap widened to 91% of market and is a secondary driver, and retention targeting hits the actual leaver group.

actions.action: Adopt the CNO's conclusion that workload interventions failed and stop them.
actions.rationale: The matched comparison contradicts it, and notice-period lags explain the early Q1 reading.

actions.action: Speed up hiring or redesign recruitment pipeline.
actions.rationale: Time-to-hire evidence is thin and hires have been steady; withdrawal data is missing.

actions.action: Reduce agency use to improve patient safety.
actions.rationale: The fall-rate association is confounded by acuity and age and has no unit-month analysis.

nextEvidence: Extend the 4 West pilot to 2-3 more high-agency units with matched controls and track resignations over 3-4 quarters
Costed model of workload relief (educators, float charge pool) versus agency savings, plus retention data by tenure band and differential status
Applicant tracking data on candidate withdrawals by stage and reason, with competitor offer timing
output.summary: Agency spend tripled mainly through volume (77%), driven by a reinforcing loop: vacancies bring agency use, which loads charge-qualified permanent RNs with charge and orientation work, which causes resignations about two quarters later, which creates more vacancies. The market and St. Brennan's story is largely rejected, since the trend began in 2024 and only 19 of 98 known leavers went there. Pay lag is a secondary driver. The 4 West pilot worked against matched units; the CNO read it too early. The bonus, funded by cutting differentials, would likely worsen the loop. Prioritize workload relief and the Vantage renegotiation.
